one_liner: A wide-moat business worth owning, but it trades at 2.8x fair value. Interesting below about $88.

profile.what: Apple designs the iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch and AirPods, and runs the App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, Apple Pay and other services on more than two billion active devices.
profile.money: The iPhone is about half of revenue (fiscal 2025), sold at premium prices through carriers, retailers and Apple's own stores. Services are about a quarter of revenue but a much larger share of gross profit, because App Store commissions, Google's payments for default search, iCloud and subscriptions carry margins above 70%. Macs, iPads and wearables make up the rest.
profile.valued: Apple is valued on P/E and free cash flow as the most profitable consumer franchise in the world. It trades at a high multiple for mid-single-digit growth because investors prize its services revenue and its buybacks; the risks to the multiple are antitrust rulings against App Store fees and Google payments.

summary.sentence: The most profitable consumer franchise in the world, growing slowly and priced as if it were growing fast.
strengths: Services revenue grows faster and at far higher margins than hardware.
Massive buybacks shrink the share count every year.
On-device AI could spark a long upgrade cycle.
risks: At about 38x earnings with a PEG above 4, the price assumes growth that history does not show.
Regulators are targeting App Store fees and the Google search payment.
Heavy dependence on China for manufacturing and sales.
swing: App Store and Google payment rulings

meaning.what_it_does: Designs iPhones, Macs, iPads, wearables and the services that run on them.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: Hardware sales (iPhone is about half of revenue) plus a fast-growing, high-margin services business: App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, payments and search licensing.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: Over two billion active devices tie customers into an ecosystem they rarely leave; every upgrade cycle and new subscription monetises that installed base.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: A product misstep that breaks the premium brand, a regulatory hit to App Store fees or the Google search payment, or China supply-chain and demand shocks.

moat.summary: Customers pay a premium and stay because of trust in the brand and the friction of leaving an ecosystem of devices, apps and data. Samsung can out-spec an iPhone and Apple still keeps its customers.

industry.summary: Consumer hardware evolves every year, but Apple's brand means it does not need to win every spec race to keep selling. AI features are the current battleground.

management.summary: A long record of disciplined capital allocation: hundreds of billions returned through buybacks and a 94% ROIC. Equity has recovered as debt has been paid down.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of two methods: (1) Owner cash flow: $92.9B a year: free cash flow less stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). (2) Damodaran: cash flow to the firm: Sales grow 4–10% for five years, fading to 3%; operating margin held at 33%; cost of capital 9.5%. Cash added, debt subtracted. The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
